description: A palette island: a subtree drawn in one palette while the page keeps another. The scope puts the palette's class on its own element. A palette class sets variables and paints nothing, so the scope also paints the ground with the palette's base-100 and base-content. The scope provides the palette to everything below it. A component that reads the palette answers the nearest scope, and outside any scope it answers the page theme. A chart is one such reader, and so is an overlay opened from inside the island. A bare palette class on an element is a valid island for styling, and it is not a scope that readers see.

palette.description: The name of a palette the theme config declares or one registered at runtime, such as `light`. A name that is neither renders pending: no palette class and no properties, so the children inherit the page's palette, and a one-time console warning names it. The scope paints the palette as soon as that name is registered, and goes back to pending when that name is removed. The scope draws the class `arena-<palette>` on its element, or for a registered palette its polarity hook and its properties, and gives every reader below it this name.

content.description: What is drawn in the palette. The slot is optional and unguarded, because a scope holding nothing yet is still a valid island.
